parts.label: Part 2
parts.article:
Good morning, everyone, and a big welcome to Biblio Stack.
Firstly, I'll explain the plan of the store to you. The building is on seven floors and is circular, as you can see, and we're here on the ground floor in its entrance hall. Right in the centre of this floor, but behind the bookshelf so you can't see it very well from here, is our main seating area, where people are encouraged to sit and read for as long as they like.
But they're under no pressure to buy what they're reading. That's not how we operate. And if you look to your immediate left, past the first double row of shelves, you'll see piles of colourful cushions in front of the window there.
We provide those so that people can sit wherever they want. Lots of people like to sit close to the bookshelves, and if they want to sit on the floor there, we want them to be as comfortable as possible. On your right, between the two larger bookshelves, you'll see the computer bench, where our visitors can search through our entire catalogue.
We pride ourselves on being the largest bookshop in the country, so our sales assistants can't possibly know all the available titles. Although the room in front of you is dominated by the bookshelves, at the far end, just in front of the lift, you'll see that we provide a small cafe bar here too.
And just to your right, there's a door to the cloakroom, where people can leave their coats. Then after that, there's a stand where we keep a selection of local and national newspapers. Customers are welcome to browse through them, and we also have some for sale. We really want people to feel as though they're browsing through books in the comfort of their own home.
Right, now I suggest we walk slowly up through the building, and I'll give you more information as we go.
We're open 12 hours a day. We don't mind if people spend the whole day here, but leave without buying anything. Of course, we hope they'll buy something, but our purpose is to draw people in, to provide the kind of environment which makes them want to stay and read. Look at how busy each floor is, but how quiet. You may be wondering whether there are any children in the building. We debated about locating children's books on the ground floor, or halfway up the building, like the third or fourth floor, but in the end, we decided to put them on the very top level, and I can assure you it's not the least bit quiet up there.
Of course, many parents would prefer to spend time on other floors, and so we provide a supervised area for children under two in the basement, so parents can wander around the shop for a few hours and not worry. But they do have to pay for this service, because although we thought about using some of our own assistants, we decided to employ qualified nursery staff for parents' complete peace of mind.
Now, we're just passing the fiction section, and you've probably noticed a small crowd of people beginning to gather. That's because a well-known author is going to read from her latest novel. We try to hold events like this at least once or twice a week, and as you can imagine, they're very popular. We don't make a charge for people to attend, but we obviously hope that some of them will want to purchase the book after listening to part of it being read aloud.
Other events which are proving to be very popular are our workshops. Last week, we held a poetry workshop, and people came along with poems that they'd written. One of the country's best-known poets ran the workshop, and the participants read their poems aloud to him. He was kind and encouraging, and many people felt inspired by his advice. It's extremely difficult to earn your living as a professional poet, and even published poets have other jobs.
Now, we're going to take a look at our section on audiobooks.

analyses.content: 从大门入口出发，看向该楼层的正中心（center），在中央书架的后面（behind the bookshelf）就是主休息区C。
你可能会只听到“center”就想随便选，但一定要听完“behind the bookshelf”，明确是在中央短书架的后面，而且你是从最下面的 entrance 入口进入的，从而精准锁定C而不是前方的E。

The building is on seven floors and is circular, as you can see, and we're here on the ground floor in its entrance hall. Right in the center of this floor, but behind the bookshelf, so you can't see it very well from here, is our main seating area, where people are encouraged to sit and read for as long as they like. But they're under no pressure to buy what they're reading. That's not how we operate.
从入口立刻向左看（immediate left），越过第一组并排的双列书架（past the first double row），在窗户前面的区域就是F。
地图题很容易因为干扰物跟错路线，你必须严格跟随“左转”且“越过第一组并排书架”的行进绝对动作，不能停留在起点附近的无关字母上。

And if you look to your immediate left, past the first double row of shelves, you'll see piles of colored cushions in front of the window there. We provide those so that people can sit wherever they want. Lots of people like to sit close to the bookshelves, and if they want to sit on the floor there, we want them to be as comfortable as possible.
朝你的右侧看，在两个较大的环形书架中间的空隙处（between the two larger bookshelves），就是电脑台D。
不要在右侧一大堆书架里迷失，你只要抓住“on your right（在右边）”并锁定“between（在...两者之间）”这个核心方位词，就能直接把目标锁定在两个大书架之间的空隙D点。

On your right, between the two larger bookshelves, you'll see the computer bench, where our visitors can search through our entire catalog. We pride ourselves in being the largest bookshop in the country, so our sales assistants can't possibly know all the available titles.
目光直接看向地图的最远端（at the far end），正对着电梯（lift）前方的区域就是咖啡吧A。
这道题很直接，但你要快速在图表顶部找到“lift”这个大参照物，没跟上这个词就会在满屏幕的书架中跟丢。
Although the room in front of you is dominated by the bookshelves, at the far end, just in front of the lift, you'll see that we provide a small café bar here, too.
入口右侧是衣帽间（cloakroom）的门，顺着外围路线继续往后走（after that），放置报纸的架子就是H。
你可能会在G和H之间犹豫，但录音强调了是在衣帽间的门“之后（after that）”，说明你的行进路线要在图上继续延伸，所以要排除紧挨着门的G，选择更靠后的H。

And just to your right, there's a door to the cloakroom, where people can leave their coats. Then after that, there's a stand where we keep a selection of local and national newspapers. Customers are welcome to browse through them, and we also have some for sale. We really want people to feel as though they're browsing through books in the comfort of their own home.

analyses.content: 书店最终雇佣了“有资质的托儿所员工（qualified nursery staff）”来照顾孩子，完美对应专业儿童看护（professional child care）。
你可能想选A，但录音说“想过用自己的普通店员但最终没用”；也极容易想当然选B，但录音明确点出这项服务是“必须要付费的（pay for this service）”，直接一击排除了免费选项。

analyses.content: 书店举办阅读活动的目的是希望有人听完后会“想要买这本书（want to purchase the book）”，直指选项A。
你可能看都没看仔细就想选C，但录音直接用“不收门票费（don't make a charge）”一脚踢开了靠卖票赚钱的干扰，听出否定词就能果断排除。
